title: Joe Gomez says Liverpool future is uncertain: ‘Anything can happen’
content:
Joe Gomez says his future at Liverpool is uncertain as he enters the final year of his contract this summer.

The 28-year-old defender is the club’s current longest-serving player having signed from Charlton Athletic in a £6million deal during Brendan Rodgers’ managerial reign in 2015.

Gomez has helped Liverpool win an array of silverware, but injuries have restricted him to 272 appearances across 11 seasons. He’s featured 31 times (16 starts) in all competitions for Arne Slot’s side in 2025-26 but has only started six Premier League matches.

Asked about his future beyond this season, Gomez said: “I think anything can happen. I don’t know is the honest answer. I’ve only got a year left so I don’t know but whatever is meant to be will be, I guess. But I’m so grateful to have had this time here at this club.

“I’ll always be grateful to have had 11 years at a place like this. All I can do is be thankful and we’ll see.”

Gomez, who has filled in at right-back at times, has largely provided cover for the first-choice centre-back duo of Virgil van Dijk and Ibrahima Konate this season.

However, Liverpool options in that area will be bolstered this summer by the arrival of £60m French defender Jeremy Jacquet from Rennes, while Italian centre-back Giovanni Leoni is returning to fitness after a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament injury wrecked his debut season on Merseyside.

There are also high hopes for young Senegalese defender Mor Talla Ndiaye, who arrived from Amitie FC for £1m in January and has been on the bench for the past two matches.

Gomez’s situation is likely to be influenced by what happens with Konate, whose contract expires at the end of June. Konate indicated after the Merseyside derby in April that he was set to pen an extension to stay at Anfield but nearly a month on, terms still haven’t been finalised and uncertainty persists.

Joe Gomez is a hugely popular figure — both in the dressing room and among the fanbase.

Capped 15 times by England, his quality has never been in doubt and he would have clocked up hundreds more appearances for Liverpool over the past decade but for the misfortune he’s faced with injuries.

Gomez came close to leaving two years ago when a fee of £45m was agreed with Newcastle United. It was dependent on Anthony Gordon heading in the opposite direction for £75million, but Newcastle pulled the plug on those deals when they managed to raise funds by selling other players to satisfy the Premier League’s profit and sustainability rules.

Last summer there was strong interest from AC Milan but the collapse of Marc Guehi’s proposed move from Crystal Palace to Liverpool meant that Gomez stayed put.

Since Slot took over Gomez has largely remained a back-up option with a total of 12 league starts across the past two seasons.

If Gomez is keen for more regular game time and there’s a decent offer on the table, it would make sense for Liverpool to bank a fee from selling him this summer rather than losing him for nothing in 12 months.

However, one understandable concern would be the prospect of losing yet another experienced player who knows what it takes to win the biggest prizes. Mohamed Salah and Andy Robertson are preparing to wave goodbye later this month, while long-serving No 1 Alisson is being pursued by Serie A outfit Juventus.
